Rashi on Nedarim 47a:1:1.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr>: בעי אבימי, קונם בית זה שאתה נכנס, ומת או שמכרו לאחר, מהו:
Rashi on Nedarim 47a:1:1.english: This is the reading: Avimi raises a dilemma: "Konam [is] this house that you enter," and he died or sold it to another, what is [the halakha]?

Rashi on Nedarim 47a:1:2.hebrew: אדם אוסר דבר וכו' - ואפילו לאחר שמת או שמכרו לאחר, הוי נמי אסור, או לא:
Rashi on Nedarim 47a:1:2.english: A person renders an item, etc. - And even after he died or sold it to another, is it also forbidden, or not?

Rashi on Nedarim 47a:3:1.english: We learned there - Later, in the chapter [entitled] HaNoder Min HaYarak.

Rashi on Nedarim 47a:3:2.hebrew: קונם פירות האלו עלי או קונם הן לפי או קונם הן על פי אסור בחילופיהן - אם נתחלפו בפירות אחרות, ודבר שלא בא לעולם הוא:
Rashi on Nedarim 47a:3:2.english: "These fruits are konam upon me," or "They are konam for my mouth," or "They are konam upon my mouth," he is prohibited from [benefiting from] their replacements - [Meaning,] if they were exchanged for other fruits, and it is something that has not [yet] come into the world.

Rashi on Nedarim 47a:3:3.english: Their growths - That one planted them and they grew.

Rashi on Nedarim 47a:4:1.english: For so-and-so - That he forbade them to his fellow.

Rashi on Nedarim 47a:4:2.hebrew: מהו - אי הוי אסור בחילופיהן כמו שהוא אסור, אי לא? מי אמרינן: גביה דיליה, כי אמר קונם הן לפי או על פי, אסור בחילופיהן אף על גב דהוי דבר שלב"ל, הואיל ואשכחן גבי דיליה כי האי חומרא דאיהו אוס' פירות חבירו עליו, ואהכי מחמירי' לגביה דאוסר נמי עליו דבר שלב"ל. אבל גבי חבירו, הואיל ואינו אוסר פירות חבירו על חבירו — דאי אמר לחבירו קונם פירות של פלוני עליך, לא הוי כלום — לא אמרינן נמי דאית בידו למיסר ליה בחליפין, דהוי דבר שלא בא לעולם:
Rashi on Nedarim 47a:4:2.english: What is [the law] - whether he [the other person] is forbidden [from] their replacements just as he [the vower himself] is forbidden, or not? Do we say: With regard to himself, when he says, "They are konam to my mouth" or "upon my mouth," he is forbidden [from] their replacements even though it is something that has not yet come into the world, since we find with regard to himself such a stringency that he can forbid his fellow's produce upon himself, and therefore we are stringent regarding him that he can also forbid upon himself something that has not yet come into the world. But with regard to his fellow, since he cannot forbid his fellow's produce upon his fellow — for if he says to his fellow, "So-and-so's produce is konam upon you," it is nothing — we likewise do not say that it is within his power to forbid [him] from [the] replacements, which are something that has not yet come into the world.

Tosafot on Nedarim 47a:1:1.english: [If] he died or sold it to another, he is permitted - Because he intended to forbid [it] only while it is his.

Tosafot on Nedarim 47a:1:2.hebrew: שדה זה שאני לוקח בית זו שאני נכנס והבית שלו מת או מכרו מהו - מי אמרי': כיון דדידיה הוא, אינו יכול לאסור אלא בעודו שלו? דנהי דתנן "בית זה שאני נכנס" ומכרו, אסור — ה"מ כשמדיר עצמו מבית חבירו, דעתו לאוסרו עליו (שהרי אסרו עליו) כשאינו שלו; ומיבעיא לאבימי כשאמר בהדיא "בחייו ובמותו". ת"ש כו' — הכא לא דחי "שאני הכא דקאמר בחייו ובמותו" כדאמר לעיל, דהכא כי נמי אמר "בחייו ובמותו", מיבעיא ליה, משום דאין אדם אוסר דבר שברשותו לכשיצא מרשותו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 47a:1:2.english: This field that I am purchasing, [or] this house that I am entering, and the house is his, [and] he died or sold it, what is [the law]? - Do we say [that] since it is his, he can only render [it] forbidden while it is still his? For although we learned in the Mishnah [that if one says], "This house that I am entering," and he [i.e., the owner] sold it, it is forbidden — that applies only when he vows himself away from his fellow's house, [for then] his intention is to forbid it upon himself (since he forbade it upon himself) [even] when it is not his; whereas Avimi's dilemma is when he explicitly said, "in his lifetime and after his death." "Come and hear, etc." — Here [the Gemara] does not reject [the proof by saying], "This case is different, as he said 'in his lifetime and after his death,'" as it said above, because here, even if he said, "in his lifetime and after his death," he [still] has a dilemma, because a person cannot render an item in his possession forbidden for [the time] after it leaves his possession.

Tosafot on Nedarim 47a:3:1.english: We learned there - Later, in the chapter [entitled] HaNoder Min HaYerek:

Tosafot on Nedarim 47a:3:2.hebrew: אסור בחילופיהן - אם מכרם או החליפם, אסורין [דמיהן וחלופיהן], דחשבינן להן כהקדש ותופס דמיו; וגידולי הקדש הקדש:
Tosafot on Nedarim 47a:3:2.english: [He is] prohibited from their replacements - If he sold them or exchanged them, [their proceeds and their replacements] are prohibited, because we consider them like consecrated property [hekdesh], and it transfers [its status to] its proceeds; and what grows from consecrated property is consecrated property.

Tosafot on Nedarim 47a:4:1.hebrew: אמר קונם פירות אלו על פלוני מהו בחילופיהן - וה״ה דמיבעיא ליה (בשאר איסורין) אם מכר, מהו שיהנה המודר מן החילופין, דשמא אסור כי ההוא דלעיל דאסור בחלופיהן. וה״ה דמיבעיא ליה בשאר איסורי הנאה, כגון ערלה וכלאי הכרם, מדקמייתי למפשט בעיין ממתני' דמקדש בערלה וכלאי הכרם. וליכא לפרושי דמיבעיא ליה באיסורי הנאה מהו בחילופיהן אם מותר למוכרם בתחילה, דפשיט' דאסור, כדמוכח פרק כל שעה (פסחים דף כא:) למ״ד "לא תאכלו" איסורי הנאה משמע, מדאיצטרי' קרא למישרי נבילה למכרה לעובד כוכבים; אלמא דאסור למכור איסורי הנאה, משום דבשעת מכירה הוא נהנה מגוף האיסור, וה״ל כשרשיפא מעצי איסור. וגם אם מכרם בדיעבד, פשיטא ליה דמותרין מן התורה, כדמפרש בשלהי פרק שני דקדושין (דף נח -), דאין לך דבר שתופס דמיו אלא עבודת כוכבים ושביעית, וקאמר התם דהוו להו שני כתובים הבאים כאחד ואין מלמדין מהם שאר איסורין. וכי קמיבעיא, אם החליפן אסורין מדרבנן, כדקאמר במתניתין: "קונם פירות אלו עלי" — אסור בחילופיהן, דחילופיהן כגידוליהן; או שמא גבי דידיה הואיל ואדם אוסר כו', אבל גבי חבירו דאין אדם אוסר פירות חבירו על חבירו, אין אדם אוסר דבר שלא בא לעולם על חבירו, וה״ה בכל איסורי הנאה, ושרי. ונראה דלהכי לא קמיבעיא ליה בחליפין איסורי הנאה [לאסור לאותן] שלא החליפם, דפשיטא דשרי, כדאמר (חולין דף ד -): "חמצן של עוברי עבירה אחר הפסח מותר מיד מפני שהם מחליפין"; ולא מיבעיא ליה אלא לאותו עצמו שהחליפן, ומבעיא בהחלפתם אי קנסינן ליה ואסור ליהנות מדרבנן:
Tosafot on Nedarim 47a:4:1.english: If one said, "This produce is konam for so-and-so," what is [the halakha] with regard to their replacements? - And the same applies that he asks (regarding other prohibitions) [that] if he sold [the produce], what is [the halakha] as to whether the one under the vow may benefit from the replacements, for perhaps it is forbidden like that [case] above where he is forbidden in their replacements. And the same applies that he asks regarding other items forbidden for benefit, such as orlah and diverse kinds of the vineyard, since [the Gemara] brings [a proof] to resolve our dilemma from the Mishnah of one who betroths [a woman] with orlah and diverse kinds of the vineyard. And it is impossible to explain that he asks regarding items forbidden for benefit, "what is [the halakha] with regard to their replacements" — whether it is permitted to sell them initially, for it is obvious that it is forbidden, as is proven in the chapter [entitled] Kol Sha'ah (Pesachim 21b) according to the one who says [that] "you shall not eat" implies [a prohibition of] items forbidden for benefit, since a verse was needed to permit selling an unslaughtered animal carcass to an idolater; thus, it is forbidden to sell items forbidden for benefit, because at the time of the sale he benefits from the forbidden item itself, and it is like a stool [made] from wood of a forbidden item. And also if he sold them after the fact, it is obvious to him that they are permitted by Torah law, as [the Gemara] explains at the end of the second chapter of Kiddushin (58a), that there is no item that transfers [its prohibition to] its monetary value except idolatry and Sabbatical-year [produce], and it says there that they are two verses that come as one [to teach the same thing], and one cannot derive other forbidden items from them. And when he asks, [it is] whether if he exchanged them they are forbidden by rabbinic decree, as [the Mishnah] says in our Mishnah: "[If one says,] 'This produce is konam for me,'" he is forbidden in their replacements, because their replacements are like their growths; or perhaps with regard to himself, since a person can render [something] forbidden [to himself], etc., whereas with regard to his fellow, since a person cannot render his fellow's produce forbidden to his fellow, a person cannot render something that has not [yet] come into the world forbidden to his fellow, and the same applies to all items forbidden for benefit, and it is permitted. And it appears that for this reason he does not ask regarding replacements of items forbidden for benefit [to forbid them to those] who did not exchange them, for it is obvious that it is permitted, as [the Gemara] says (Chullin 4a): "The chametz of transgressors after Passover is permitted immediately because they exchange [it]"; and he only asks regarding that very person who exchanged them, and he asks concerning their exchange whether we penalize him and it is forbidden to benefit [from them] by rabbinic decree:
